definition: A bending moment is the internal moment developed in a structural member as a result of external loads and reactions.
physicalMeaning: It represents the tendency of forces acting on a structural member to cause it to rotate or bend.
engineeringImportance: Bending moment is fundamental to understanding flexural behaviour and is used extensively in structural analysis and design.
practicalImportance: Engineers use bending moments to understand how members respond to loading and to determine the required flexural capacity and reinforcement or section properties.
failureImplications: Reinforced concrete members may develop flexural cracking
Insufficient flexural capacity can lead to structural failure
